goal: Pick up the cup containing 7 balls, pour all the balls into the vase, put the cup back upright and bring the arms home.
instruction_templates: Pour all the balls from the cup into the vase.
success: All 7 balls sphere_0..sphere_6 are 'in' the vase: for each ball, its centre XY lies inside the footprint (convex hull of the rotated bounding box, XY) of the vase and its centre z is above the vase bbox's minimum z (no upper z bound).
The cup is upright: the cup's local +Z axis is within 15 deg (default threshold, strict) of world +Z.

Both target arms are back at origin: all target arms (left_arm and right_arm; the support arm is not counted) have their end-effector pose within 0.15 m on EACH axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| all <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angle) of the pose they had at the start of the episode (recorded after the scene settled).
evaluation: Single stage; all 9 conditions (7 balls, cup upright, arms home) must hold simultaneously after one action. The reward manager is evaluated only once per action (after the sim sub-steps of that action are finished), never between sub-steps. In each evaluation the FIRST pending stage of the check list is tested (every condition in it, all at that same moment; a condition that is a nested list is an OR); when it passes it is removed permanently (never re-verified later) and the next stage becomes pending; at most one stage is removed per action. Reward is 1.0 only when the check list is empty (and no query/trigger counter is violated); the episode is declared a success as soon as reward >= 0.999 after an action, and ends as a failure if the action counter reaches step_lim without that, or earlier if the environment is flagged failed (query counter exceeded, see below). No final_check list is registered by this task, so the final-check logic at step_lim adds nothing. No early failure condition other than the usual physics/end-flag handling.
objects: cup: a cup ('cup' category index 6) (Rigid, 1), table-frame x in [-0.4,0.4], y in [-0.2,0.05], random yaw up to +-75 deg
sphere_0..sphere_6: 7 balls (Rigid, 7) placed inside the cup at start (relative to cup xy offsets within +-0.02 m, stability check disabled, forced placement)
vase: target vase (Geometry, static, 1; one of 5 models index 0-4), table-frame x in [-0.35,0.35], y in [-0.12,0.05], random yaw up to +-45 deg
scene_dynamics: none (the balls start in the cup and only move if the cup is moved)
end_requirements: Both arms within 0.15 m per axis / 20 deg of their start pose, and the cup standing upright (<15 deg tilt), all at the same time as all 7 balls are in the vase.
physics_kind: rigid (7 small rigid spheres inside a rigid cup)
notes: The ball-in-vase test is only the ball centre's XY inside the vase footprint with z above the vase bbox bottom, so a ball resting on a vase rim or an outer rim region inside the footprint's convex hull also counts, and balls anywhere above the vase footprint count. A vase is a static Geometry object. The vase can be far from the cup. Balls dropped on the table or outside fail the all-7 requirement permanently unless re-picked (not practical). The cup must be put back upright (not left lying/tilted) before the arms return home.
